visible.author: Rusch
visible.title: 1st timer install tip, good product
visible.body: The parts are fine. There not much to em a couple blocks, spacers and some long bolts. 1) the biggest hurdle on reassembly is the lower shock mount. (with shock removed) try to spin the lower mounting hole on the shock angle in the opposite direction using a vice as the upper spacer reverses the shock.. dont be afraid to use a hammer to pop the lower bolts through and prepare to do some wrestling. The 1st shock took me 2.5 hrs with power tools. the other side took less than an hr after you get an idea of what to do. this time Included the install of Rough Country upper control arms. 2) the rear is way easier just be sure to have it jacked up high enough. when installing the new blocks you cant be afraid to pull/ wrestle/ twist the diff so that the mounting holes pop into the spring. this should take about 1.5 hrs max for a beginner. looks good for a small lift level.

low_same_part_other_truck.author: YounesYasin
low_same_part_other_truck.title: *AVOID*Missing Vital Component
low_same_part_other_truck.body: The materials used are good quality, but the fact that this kit does NOT include a differential drop makes it dangerous to use. I was unaware that this part was needed until after having the part installed, and soon after, puncturing my CV Axle. I took it to Mr. Wheels in South Florida and they informed me that a diff drop is an absolute necessity if leveling/lifting 2"+. The part is only ~$30 and can save your suspension from having issues. Avoid this product and look for one that includes the diff drop.
low_same_part_other_truck.product: Mammoth 3-Inch Front / 2-Inch Rear Leveling Kit (07-21 Tundra, Excluding TRD Pro)

Lone story short my 23 Tacoma with 1500 miles on it (200 miles with this sh*t leveling kit) blew my differential seal because of the steep angle on the driver side....Buy something complete and pass on this half assed level kit......the install and all the repairs have cost me 12x the price of this kit.....
